source_documents.title: Illuminating Olympicenes: Insights Into Anti‐Kasha Photophysics in Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons

reference_evidence_units.quote: Spectroscopic evidence demonstrates these behaviors arise from multiple singlet emissive states—an anti-Kasha locally excited (LE) state (Sn , n ≥ 2) and an intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four olympicenes
reference_evidence_units.statement: Dual fluorescence: an anti-Kasha LE band and an ICT band.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Such spectral variations clearly support the occurrence of an ICT process in all olympicene derivatives.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Polarity-induced red shifts and band redistribution in absorption and emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Only qualitative solvatochromism; no Lippert-Mataga analysis or CT calculation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Moreover, viscosity-dependent fluorescence emission measurements rule out the formation of a twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) state, indicating the process is ICT rather than TICT (Figures S15–S18).
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission does not depend on viscosity: planar ICT, not TICT.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This “anomalous” phenomenon suggests that the blueshifted emissive bands likely originate from the higher excited state (Sn , n ≥ 2), indicative of anti-Kasha behavior. In contrast, the redshifted emissive bands are attributed to ICT emission, reflecting the strong charge-transfer character of these olympicene derivatives.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: The blue band overlaps higher absorption bands (Sn emission); the red band is ICT emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Most importantly, the blueshifted emissive bands, in the range 350 nm (28571 cm−1 ) to 450 nm (20202 cm−1 ), are not excitation-dependent, indicating a LE state. Conversely, the redshifted emissive bands exhibit conspicuous excitation-dependent fluorescence, which strongly supports an ICT state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Excitation dependence separates the LE and ICT bands.

reference_evidence_units.quote: All of the examined olympicene derivatives exhibit pronounced excitation-dependent emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: Oly-one, tBu-MeOly-ol, (HxO)2-Oly-one

reference_evidence_units.quote: The LE emission bands are also suppressed, influenced by π-π interaction between the olympicene cores, likely due to aggregation. An exception to this occurrence is tBu-MeOly-ol, which shows higher- and lower-energy emission features.
reference_evidence_units.subject: solid samples
reference_evidence_units.statement: In the solid the LE band is suppressed by core pi-pi interaction, except for tBu-MeOly-ol.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Stated as likely; solid-state study left for later work.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The multiple decay components are attributed to fluorescence from the LE state and/or the fully or partially relaxed ICT state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four

reference_evidence_units.quote: These observations demonstrate that molecular oxygen plays a moderate fluorescence-quenching role in these olympicene systems, with integrated fluorescence intensities approximately 1.3–1.9 times larger after degassing (Figures S19–S22).
reference_evidence_units.subject: all four
reference_evidence_units.statement: Moderate oxygen quenching of the fluorescence.

reference_evidence_units.quote: largely attributed to the two hexyl-oxy groups’ strong electron-donating character reducing the HOMO-LUMO gap.
reference_evidence_units.subject: (HxO)2-Oly-one
reference_evidence_units.statement: The most red-shifted S0-S1 band comes from the two alkoxy donors.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The red, excitation-dependent fluorescence band is assigned to a planar ICT state (solvatochromism; viscosity independence rules out TICT). Evidence is qualitative: no Lippert-Mataga analysis or excited-state calculation.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: In the solid, pi-pi interaction between the cores suppresses the LE band (stated as likely).

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Rigidity is discussed for vibronic structure in absorption; viscosity measurements are used only to exclude TICT.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The red, excitation-dependent fluorescence band is assigned to a planar ICT state (solvatochromism; viscosity independence rules out TICT). Evidence is qualitative: no Lippert-Mataga analysis or excited-state calculation.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: In the solid, pi-pi interaction between the cores suppresses the LE band (stated as likely).

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The anti-Kasha LE emission is identified but not explained by state order, gaps or rates (recorded out of pool).

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_ISC_RTP_TADF
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Oxygen quenching of the fluorescence is reported; no triplet state is invoked.

environment_context: oxygen: moderate fluorescence quenching (1.3-1.9x brighter after degassing) (E09)
